long_narrative: Born into rock royalty but determined to chart his own course, Will Johns grew up surrounded by legendary figures in British music. The son of famed producer Andy Johns—who worked with Led Zeppelin and The Rolling Stones—and the nephew of Eric Clapton, Will’s early life unfolded in a blur of guitars, studio sessions, and backstage passes. Yet, despite his lineage, he carved his identity the hard way—through clubs, pubs, and indie blues circuits. Having battled personal demons, including addiction and self-doubt, music became his sanctuary. His sound blends British blues traditions with modern vulnerability, guitar grit, and heartfelt vocals. Over the years, he’s played over 200 shows worldwide, collaborated with icons, judged guitar contests, and advocated for mental health and recovery. Will Johns isn’t just keeping the blues alive—he’s redefining it.

long_narrative: Anslom Nakikus, born Ronald Nakikus on Matupit Island, PNG, grew up surrounded by music, performing with the Barike Band as a teen. Over two decades, he has released multiple albums, blending reggae’s core themes with Pacific cultural roots. His international breakthrough came with Love Me Again (2019), recorded with Lucky Dube’s band. In 2024, he became the first PNG artist to sign with a major label (Kingmaker/Universal), releasing One Love with reggae legends Chaka Demus and Quino. A cultural ambassador and advocate, Anslom uses his music for refugee rights, HIV/AIDS awareness, and youth empowerment, performing at global festivals including Expo 2020 Dubai, One Love Festival Jamaica, and FestPAC Hawaii. He continues to bridge local authenticity with global reach.

long_narrative: Sami Chohfi’s journey bridges cultures, music, and human stories. Born to a Brazilian mother and Middle Eastern father, he grew up between traditions, fueling his empathy and artistic worldview. Starting as frontman of alternative rock band Blue Helix, he earned success in the U.S. and Brazil before shifting to a solo career with the album Extraordinary World (2020), written and filmed across six countries. His work blends emotional alternative rock with culturally rich visuals, often tackling themes like loneliness, resilience, and identity. Beyond music, Sami is committed to mental health awareness, cultural inclusion, and cross-border unity. He continues to tour globally, engage deeply with fans, and produce authentic, independent art.

long_narrative: Lyia Meta’s journey spans from Malaysia’s blues clubs to Grammy-nominated collaborations. A multi-genre vocalist, visual artist, and writer, she has built a global reputation for emotional authenticity and fearless creativity. Her breakout single 'Always You' earned multiple awards including the Cannes Music Award, and in 2024 her voice featured on a Grammy-nominated album. As a Lazie Indie Magazine columnist, she has conducted 33 interviews and authored six cover stories, championing indie voices worldwide. Lyia merges music with visual art, creating immersive storytelling experiences that reflect her belief that authenticity is the most radical art of all.
